newsitem.title: USA: Northern Telecom sells part of unit.
newsitem.headline: Northern Telecom sells part of unit.

text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd said it sold off part of a unit that targets the secure network industry by providing infrastructure software products for the encryption and digital signature of information.

The companyu said it will own a majority stake in newly-formed Entrust Technologies, which will be based in Ottawa, Ontario. Entrust will carry on the business of Northern Telecom's Secure Networks unit.

Olympus Partners Inc, J.P. Morgan Investment Management, Societe Generale, T. Rowe Price Threshold Funds and Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette have bought about $26 million of the new company's common stock in a private placement, Nortel said.
Nortel did not disclose the unit's annual revenue or say what revenue it would contribute to Nortel as a partially spun-off company, a Nortel spokesman said.
Nortel formed the unit in 1993 to market and develop data security software for corporate enterprises.
Nortel is a Canada-based telecommunications company.
